observed_title: Asymptotics of the rate function in the large deviation principle for sums of independent identically distributed random variables
version: Electronic Communications in Probability 29 (2024), article 12, pp.1–6; DOI 10.1214/24-ECP584

read_ranges.scope: 全文：LDP/rate-function preliminaries、Proposition 1、Theorem 2 完整证明、Remarks 3–4、全部参考文献。

topic_relevance.H04: direct for the exact large-deviation rate-function component: establishes when the iid Cramér rate function asymptotically matches the log one-step tail. It does not provide a variance-stratified theorem or a finite-n exact tail approximation.

definitions.name: Cramér rate function and LDP tail exponent
definitions.statement: For iid X_i with Λ(t)=ln E e^{tX}, Λ*(y)=sup_{t∈R}{ty−Λ(t)}; the LDP exponent for P(S_n≥nx) is ℓ(x)=−inf_{y≥x}Λ*(y). In the nontrivial positive-mgf case, Λ* grows at infinity and eventually ℓ(x)=−Λ*(x).

definitions.name: one-step log-tail
definitions.statement: q(x)=P(X≥x), L(x)=ln q(x), with ln0=−∞. The relation L(x)∼L0(x) is asymptotic ratio equivalence for an eventually finite, nonzero log-tail and a real-valued concave L0.

definitions.name: Bernstein–Chernoff bound objective
definitions.statement: Q(x,t)=e^{−tx}M(t), M(t)=E e^{tX}; for t≥0, q(x)≤Q(x,t). A carefully selected quasi-minimizer of Q yields the upper asymptotic needed in the sufficiency argument.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 2 (characterization of rate-function/tail equivalence)
assumptions: X,X_1,X_2,… are iid; define Λ and Λ* as in (2).
The nontrivial case: Λ(t_1)<∞ for some t_1>0; otherwise Proposition 1 yields Λ*(y)→0 and ℓ(x)=0 for x≥0.
theorem_cards.statement: The asymptotic relation −Λ*(x)∼L(x) as x→∞ holds if and only if L(x)∼L_0(x) for some real-valued concave function L_0 (equivalently Λ*(x)∼−ln P(X≥x)).
proof_steps: Necessity: choose L_0=−Λ* eventually; Λ* is convex, hence −Λ* is concave.
Sufficiency: let g=−L and g_0=−L_0. Concavity of L_0 makes g_0 convex/increasing eventually; define A(x)=c g_0(x)/g_0'(x), k(x)=inf_{v≥x−A} g(v)/g_0(v)→1, and t_x=(c k(x)g_0(x)−1)/A(x), with c∈(0,1).

Use integration by parts to write M(t)=t∫e^{tv}q(v)dv and split at x−A into I_1+I_2. Convexity gives g_0(v)≥g_0(x)+g_0'(x)(v−x); this bounds e^{−t_x x}I_2 by q(x)^{1+o(1)} and e^{−t_x x}I_1 by q(x)^{c+o(1)}, then let c approach 1 to get the matching upper log bound.
The Bernstein–Chernoff inequality gives the reverse bound ℓ(x)≥L(x), completing equivalence.
gaps: The conclusion is an asymptotic equivalence for an LDP rate function versus the one-step log-tail; it is not a finite-sample relative approximation or a Gaussian/moderate-deviation theorem.
No variance stratification is present; the H04 direct assignment covers the exact rate-function component only.
The argument uses the standard iid LDP formulation and does not independently establish a general LDP for dependent or triangular-array inputs.

constant_dependence: Asymptotic statement only; no explicit finite-n numerical constant. The proof’s c∈(0,1) is an auxiliary asymptotic parameter tending to 1, not a universal error constant.
endpoint_limits: A positive mgf exists at at least one t_1>0 in the nontrivial case.
The concave equivalent L_0 must be real-valued eventually; the theorem does not cover a tail with log-probability remaining −∞.
reusable_methods: A convex conjugate rate function can be compared to the original one-step tail through a controlled near-minimizer of the Chernoff objective.
For a target model, first verify the iid LDP and concave-equivalent log-tail hypotheses; do not infer finite-n or variance-layer precision from this asymptotic characterization.
unchecked: The note is six pages and was fully read; this is not an independent proof audit of the cited general LDP theorem.
No transfer to variance-stratified dependent fields has been proved.
